caveats: No official Moonton Season 7.1 patch notes covering economy were found in this pass; Season 7.1-specific observations come from LoadoutGG's Season 7.1 coverage.
LoadoutGG states its data is extracted from game files and official sources but it is not affiliated with Moonton.
TheDiplomatRiot (Dec 2025) interest figures conflict with all other sources and are treated as an outlier.
ARCTopup leveling pacing (L4 R6 / L5 R9 / L6 R13 / L7 R17 / L8-9 R21+) remains unverified and sits in meta_comps.json; it is not repeated as fact here.

auto_exp_per_round.note: Classic figure from the Fandom wiki (commander gains 2 EXP each round; gold can also be exchanged for EXP). GamingOnPhone confirms Go Go keeps Magic Chess's core mechanics, but no Season 7.1 source restated this number.

max_level.note: LoadoutGG's Season 7.1 economy guide is explicitly about 'when to stop at level 9 or push 10'; a Season 7-era Lancelot gameplay video shows a player reaching Level 10. Level 9 is described as the normal checkpoint.

commander_level.xp_costs_note: No source found for the gold/EXP cost of commander levels 4-10 in Season 7.1. A commander-specific Season 7 video shows: Level 5 before Round I-3, Level 9 by Round III-1, then push 10 (Lancelot fast-level example, not universal). ARCTopup's pacing (L4 R6 / L5 R9 / L6 R13 / L7 R17 / L8-9 R21+) is already recorded as unverified in meta_comps.json and conflicts with LoadoutGG's Season 7.1 'level 9 checkpoint' framing.

interest.conflict: thediplomariot.com (Dec 2025) claims 1 gold per 10 saved, max 3 at 30+ gold. Single outlier; all other sources agree on 2 per 10 capped at 4.
interest.note: 10 gold -> +2, 20 gold -> +4, cap +4. Corroborated across classic and Go Go-era sources, and consistent with LoadoutGG's Season 7.1 reference to 'the 20-gold line' (the cap is reached at 20 gold). NOT from official Season 7.1 patch notes.
sources: lichessdude.com/magic-chess-go-go-hidden-strategy (Go Go-specific: bonus gold for every 10 gold saved; keep 10/20/30)
loadoutgg.com/magic-chess-gogo (Season 7.1 guide description: 'the interest table, the 20-gold line')

streak_bonus.note: Multiple sources confirm extra gold is paid for consecutive wins AND consecutive losses (noypigeeks, lichessdude, BlueStacks level-up guide), but no source found in this pass published the exact per-streak table for Season 7.1.

win_bonus_gold.note: Classic Magic Chess figure (+1 gold per round win) from the Fandom wiki. Carried over by most guides but never confirmed in a Season 7.1 source.

meta.best_source_for_season_7_1: LoadoutGG Magic Chess: GoGo hub + its Season 7.1 guides (data extracted from game files per their statement; guide bodies not machine-readable in this research pass, only the Season 7.1-scoped descriptions were captured)
meta.data_policy: JANGAN karang angka: every numeric field without a citable source is null and listed under unverified_flags. Legacy/classic-Magic-Chess figures are kept only as labeled legacy references, never as current Season 7.1 values.

season_7_1_changes.change: Level 9 checkpoint vs pushing Level 10 is framed as the central late-game economy decision.
Interest table and the 20-gold line remain the core banking mechanic; LoadoutGG dedicates a Season 7.1 guide section to it.
Economy Go Go Cards are a Season 7.1 decision point ('which Go Go Cards pay').
New commander Brody turns spare heroes into 5-cost ones (economy-adjacent: converts bench gold into high-cost units).
Equipment and safety-net commanders lead the Season 7.1 meta (context for which economy plans are viable).

Magic Auction is a separate Season 7.1 mode with its own bidding economy: how a round and a win work, bid sizing, the Secret Auction House, keeping vs selling Treasures, six ranks, and 18 Auction commander skills.

shop.odds_note: No source found for Season 7.1 shop odds per commander level. LoadoutGG's Season 7.1 economy guide covers 'the shop odds and shared pool' but the guide body was not machine-readable in this pass. Leveling advice that depends on odds (3-cost reroll vs 4-cost board vs legend rush wanting different levels) is recorded qualitatively under strategies.

reroll_cost_gold.note: Classic figure (2 gold per manual shop refresh). No Season 7.1 source restated it.

shared_pool.note: LoadoutGG confirms a shared shop pool exists in Season 7.1. Only published per-hero copy counts are classic-era Fandom figures: Normal 27 / Good 21 / Elite 18 / Epic 13 / Legendary 9. Unverified for Season 7.1.

slots_per_round.note: Classic figure (5 heroes offered per round). No Season 7.1 source restated it.

example.plan: Level 5 before Round I-3 to maximize gold income; rush Level 9 (reached by Round III-1 in the example), then push Level 10 for a 10-slot board. Lancelot's kit de-emphasizes interest in favor of flat gold.
example.source: youtube.com/watch?v=YPmLmATS9Eg (Season 7-era gameplay, commander-specific - not a universal curve)

strategies.name: Fast level (aggressive)
sources: bluestacks.com MCGG level-up guide (slow/fast/balanced levelling strategies)
strategies.summary: Spend gold on commander EXP early to hit higher levels first, build an early board lead, and snowball win-streak income. Risky if you lose early rounds because the spent gold is gone.

strategies.name: Slow level / economy build
sources: noypigeeks.com (keep at least 20 gold for +4 interest; never drop below 10 when spending)
strategies.summary: Save gold, spend minimal gold on EXP and rerolls, bank at interest breakpoints (10/20 gold) and level up naturally while the banked gold compounds.

strategies.name: Balanced
strategies.summary: Mix fast and slow leveling based on board strength and streak state: bank interest while staying competitive, push Level 7-8 by mid-game.

strategies.name: Reroll discipline
sources: thediplomariot.com (reroll only near an upgrade/synergy; avoid uncontrolled rerolls)
lichessdude.com (only re-roll heavily if you absolutely need specific heroes; save early)
strategies.summary: Do not reroll aggressively early; only reroll when close to a key star upgrade or synergy breakpoint. Uncontrolled rerolling breaks the interest bank and stalls the game plan.

strategies.name: Interest breakpoints
strategies.summary: Keep banked gold at multiples of 10; the key Season 7.1 line is 20 gold for the maximum +4 interest. Spend down to 10 (not below) only when a purchase is worth more than the lost interest; rebuild to 20 after.

strategies.name: Match your level plan to your carry cost
sources: loadoutgg.com/magic-chess-gogo (Season 7.1 hub: 'Decide the plan before the gold goes out... a 3-cost re-roll, a 4-cost board and a legend rush each want different levels')
strategies.summary: Decide the plan before spending: a 3-cost reroll comp, a 4-cost board, and a legend (5-cost) rush each want different commander levels, and the chosen commander usually points to one of them. The Season 7.1 decision is the level 9 checkpoint vs pushing 10.

strategies.name: Economy commanders and Go Go Cards
sources: roonby.com (Lancelot: 1 gold win / 2 gold loss + bonus chance, at the cost of interest)
bluestacks.com MCGG level-up guide (Chou, Benny, Eva, Lukas as economy/leveling commanders)
loadoutgg.com/magic-chess-gogo (Season 7.1: 'which Go Go Cards pay'; new commander Brody turns spare heroes into 5-cost ones)
strategies.summary: Some commanders are economy engines: Lancelot gives flat gold for wins AND losses but forfeits interest; Chou gives extra gold every round; Benny can grant free EXP; Eva boosts hero strength and economy; Lukas rewards win streaks. During creep rounds, prioritize Go Go Cards that pay (economy cards such as Payday and Jump the Gun+ are called out in Season 7 gameplay). Season 7.1 adds Brody, who turns spare heroes into 5-cost ones.

strategies.name: Lose-streak leverage (legacy)
sources: noypigeeks.com (losing streak gold bonus + first pick at Choice of Fate)
strategies.summary: Consecutive losses pay streak gold and (in classic Magic Chess) gave first pick at Choice of Fate for capacity/equipment/emblem/hero. Unverified whether the pick-order mechanic still exists in Season 7.1.

unverified_flags: strategies.lose_streak_leverage (legacy mechanic, pick-order part unverified for S7.1)
